# Report: `region.fasta` (>region_002, 3,000 bp)

**Bottom line:** the sequence is largely featureless except for one clear, striking structure — a **tandem repeat array spanning ~1345–1771**, built from seven 61-bp units in perfect phase. Details below.

## Key feature: tandem repeat array, positions 1345–1771 (~427 bp)

The array consists of **seven tandem copies of a 61-bp period** (427 bp = 7 × 61), with an invariant **26-bp conserved core** at the start of each full unit:

> **TTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAACAC**

The core occurs **six times at exact 61-bp periodicity** at:
- **1406–1431, 1467–1492, 1528–1553, 1589–1614, 1650–1675, 1711–1736**

Copy #1 (1345–1405) is **degenerate**: its 5′ segment matches the core only partially (`TTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAACTC…`). The last ~35 bp of each unit are **variable** between copies (only 26 of 61 columns are identical across the array), and all six variable segments end in **…GG** immediately before the next core. The array is flanked by non-repetitive sequence on both sides (unique sequence resumes at 1772).

This architecture — a conserved repeat core with variable intervening segments — is reminiscent of a **CRISPR-like repeat/spacer array** (26-ish-bp repeat + ~35-bp spacer) or, more mundanely, a **degenerate minisatellite**. Resolution would require a database search (BLAST of the 26-mer, checking for adjacent cas genes or a leader sequence); no adjacent coding genes are evident.

**Coding context:** one reading frame is open from **1389 to 1757** (122 codons, no stop), spanning the whole array. However, the repeat is unlikely to be protein-coding: the 61-bp period is not a multiple of 3 (61 = 3×20+1), so the six conserved cores fall in **all three reading frames** across the array, and the putative ORF lacks an ATG start and any Shine–Dalgarno-like context. The core simply happens to contain no stop codons in any frame.

## Secondary observations (minor)

- **Composition:** overall GC 43.6% (A 29.6%, T 26.8%), with strong local heterogeneity in 200-bp windows — from **~24% GC (1001–1200)** to **~59% GC (1401–1600, the repeat block)**. The 950–1250 region is AT/TA-rich filler-like sequence.
- **Restriction sites:** HindIII ×3 (132, 1082, 2607), SpeI (852), ClaI (1218), PstI (2181). No EcoRI, BamHI, or other common sites.
- No long homopolymers, no obvious −10/−35 promoter motifs, no long palindromic/hairpin-forming segments detected on inspection. The exact round length (3,000 bp) suggests a curated/in-silico segment.

## Conclusion

The only notable feature is the **7-copy, 61-bp degenerate tandem repeat at 1345–1771** with a perfectly conserved 26-bp core (first full copy at 1406–1466; conserved core copies at 1406, 1467, 1528, 1589, 1650, 1711). The remainder of the sequence — apart from compositional heterogeneity — appears unremarkable, with no compelling ORFs or other motifs.
